PreparedStatement.doc: A compiled SQL statement ready for repeated execution. `program` is the bytecode produced by the per-statement compiler. `arity` is the count of distinct anonymous `?` placeholders observed by the parser, equal to the max 1-based Param.idx in the parsed AST (0 if none). Targets MAY add target-private fields (e.g. a cached VdbeState for warm reuse) so long as the public observable behavior matches Pins 1-7 in master.md.

BoundParams.doc: Caller-side bind-parameter slot vector. Sized to a PreparedStatement's arity at construction; every slot is initialized to Value::Null. `bind` overwrites a single slot. The vector is positional; slot k (1-based) lives at `values[k-1]`. The vector is owned by the caller (or by the target's PreparedStatement wrapper) and copied into the per-step VdbeState by `step`.

StepResult.doc: Outcome of a `step` call. v1 emits Done at end of program (run-to-completion); the Row variant is reserved for the v1.1 pause-on-ResultRow iterator surface but is part of the v1 shape so target mappings don't need a wire-shape change at v1.1.

Row.doc: v1.1: a row is available; the caller reads it via the program's row_sink (or a target-specific row accessor) and calls step again.

Done.doc: Program reached Halt(Ok). For row-producing SELECTs, this means every row has been delivered via the row_sink. For INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL, this is the success terminator.

Error.doc: Program halted with an error condition.

PrepareError.doc: Failure modes of `prepare`. ParseFailure wraps the parser's ParseError; CompileFailure wraps the per-statement compiler's CompileError. Targets render this as the canonical sum-of-errors (Rust enum, Go untagged, etc.).

BindError.doc: Failure modes of `bind`. SlotOutOfRange covers slot < 1 or slot > arity (slot is 1-based, see Pin 2). Targets MAY render the variant as a single-case error type carrying both fields if a wider error surface is unwanted.

StepError.doc: Distinct from StepResult::Error so the lib-api surface can preserve a non-Result step return signature (e.g. an iterator yielding StepResult). For targets that prefer a Result-shaped step, StepError is the err alternative; for targets emitting StepResult directly, StepError is unused.

BoundParams.name: for_arity
BoundParams.doc: Construct a BoundParams vector sized to `arity`, initialized to `arity` copies of Value::Null. arity == 0 yields an empty vector. The returned vector pairs with a PreparedStatement of the same arity; mismatched pairings are a caller bug (no spec-side check; the per-step copy loop iterates 0..arity).

prepare.doc: Parse, compile, and arity-determine a single SQL statement. The `db` borrow is used for schema-registry lookup at compile time (table / view / index name resolution). Returns Ok(stmt) on success; ParseFailure or CompileFailure on the corresponding error. Multi-statement input (semicolon-separated) is NOT admitted in v1: the function consumes the first statement and the parser surfaces an error if non-whitespace trails the statement terminator.

bind.doc: Install `value` at slot (1-based) in the caller's BoundParams vector. Pins: see master.md Pin 2. Slot 0 or slot > stmt.arity yields Err(SlotOutOfRange); within range, the prior value (Null on first call, prior bound value on subsequent calls) is replaced.

step.doc: Execute the prepared statement against `db` with the current `params`. Constructs a fresh VdbeState sized to the statement's program, calls set_params_arity(stmt.arity) + per-slot set_param to seed the bind-parameter slots from `params.values`, then calls execute_program. Returns StepResult::Done on Halt(Ok), StepResult::Error(cond) on a runtime condition. Row materialization happens via the program's row_sink callback (see master.md §Algorithm); the v1.1 pause-on-row surface will return StepResult::Row before completion. Caller is responsible for fresh-state semantics: each step constructs a new VdbeState; reuse + reset is achievable via a target-specific cached-state path that does NOT change observable behavior.

reset.doc: Discard per-step VdbeState (PC, cursors, aggregate / window slots, buffer slots). Bindings (the `params` vector) are PRESERVED; the next step starts from PC 0 with the same params. v1's spec-side reset is a no-op (since `step` allocates a fresh state every call) — the function exists to pin the contract and to give targets that DO cache a per-statement VdbeState a hook for the discard. Targets that don't cache state implement reset as () / no-op.
